input.rationale: A Vendor-side IP infringement indemnity is present in Section 13 (headed "INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY INDEMNITY", continuing at p0090-p0093). It is framed as an indemnity for breach of an IP ownership/non-infringement warranty rather than using the words "infringe or misappropriate", but it is substantively an IP indemnity running from Garman to us: (i) Garman "represents and warrants that it owns or controls all rights necessary to grant the rights to Sparkling" and that no lien, encumbrance, security interest or other third-party rights against the Work will interfere with our rights; (ii) "Garman agrees to indemnify Sparkling and hold it harmless from any and all losses, damages and expenses", expressly including court costs, arbitration fees, amounts paid in settlement of claims and reasonable legal fees, incurred by us or our officers and directors due to breach of that warranty; and (iii) the quoted language supplies the customary infringement remedies - where the Work "is held to constitute an infringement of another Person's rights, and use thereof is enjoined", Garman must at its own election and expense procure the right to use, procure an equivalent element, or replace/modify (p0091-p0093). There is no reciprocal or one-way Sparkling indemnity anywhere in the agreement, and Section 15 states that the damages limitation "shall not apply to breaches of Sections 13 and 14", so the Vendor indemnity is uncapped - better than the fallback's 3x annual fees super-cap and plainly not walk-away territory. The clause therefore meets the fallback position (Vendor IP indemnity with customary remedies, and without the usual customer-modification/combination exclusions), so it is compliant and we do not redline it. Noted short of preferred but not material enough to flag: no express duty to defend or control the defence, no refund remedy, no extension to Vendor's breach of law, Vendor-caused unauthorised access to Customer Data or gross negligence/wilful misconduct, and a ten calendar day claim-notice period tighter than our usual "prompt notice" standard.
